recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Neural pathways inside, etheric pathways outside", "body": "Chance reads Michael's formula aloud: just as hypnosis can establish neural pathways in the brain, what we call magic can establish etheric pathways in the world. Michael describes neural pathways as entrained routes linking a thought to a behaviour, laid by experience, repetition and strong emotion and set off again by anything symbolically similar, recalling touching his face in the mirror whenever he rehearsed a line he did not believe. Applying as above so below, he maps rivers onto the body's veins and arteries and argues that what he calls the planet's oldest river, the Susquehanna, anchors the first expressions of computing, globalism and wired electricity."}, {"title": "Skill that spreads through the collective", "body": "Chance says he first sensed a link between personal patterns and a collective field at music festivals, watching the average level of hula hoopers rise each year as more people practised, and he points to climbers who now free climb in hours big walls that first took weeks. He pictures skills as tunnels others have already dug. Michael calls flow arts, festivals and climbing the most human things imaginable, set against war as the most unhuman, and argues for a split where 20 percent competition brings out our best. In his outro Chance adds Rupert Sheldrake's morphic fields and a rat maze experiment he remembers hearing about."}, {"title": "Inception as a map of the dream", "body": "Michael rewatched Inception and reads it as a model of an engineered reality: a machine hosts the shared dream, its maze is designed by a psychology student rather than a coder, lucid dreamers work the mark, and when the subconscious senses something is wrong a second dream waits behind the first. He links this to Gnostic ideas of an archonic false reality, to Truthstream Media's Minds of Men on the cybernetics movement, and to the internet as the ultimate machine. Chance adds his idea of controlled awakenings, citing the Protestant Reformation and the QAnon phenomenon as moments where people thought they woke up but were steered into a new worldview."}, {"title": "Michael's hundred year plan theory", "body": "Michael describes what he calls a hundred year plan that began with the first computer, arguing that anyone born since 1945 has been hooked on the culture and technology of their earliest years. He ties the present moment to Jupiter and Saturn moving into Aquarius with Pluto to follow, and says the pressure now is to get people to commit to an inverted, anti-human expression of the Age of Aquarius, which he calls Robosapien rather than human. Because force would incur karma, he argues this dream runs on loopholes, and Chance asks whether a mass inception is steering the manifesting power of millions of imaginations toward a chosen outcome."}, {"title": "Navigating the dream as a human", "body": "Michael's approach to navigating the dream starts with separating human nature from second nature, which he describes as a learned neural pathway, and then tracing anything made back to its origins to ask whether it is in harmony with being human. Computers are his main example: he values being able to talk with Chance across distance but argues the industry rests on a foundation of decay, from rare metal extraction to slave labour. He says the trivium's rational mind must come before the quadrivium's imagination, and that waking up means getting back into the body through dancing, yoga, climbing and flow arts."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Michael Wann is a synchromystic researcher who uncovers occult correlations and connections between cultural phenomenon and our individual experience. In this episode we look at the movie Inception and what it reveals about the digital dream-world that humanity has mistaken for reality, the relationship between human neural pathways and macro-cosmic patterns in the universal mind, and the harvesting of the mass-imagination for the manifestation of a totalitarian age.
